proof_summary: For every \(1\le d\le2025\), an lcm case analysis shows that one of \((2,17),(3,17),(5,23),(7,19),(11,13)\) consists of two primes not dividing \(d\); each pair has distinct final digits and product at most \(150\). Since \(d\) is invertible modulo that product, some index below the product makes \(a+id\) divisible by both primes, so one of the first \(150\) terms fails the required condition.
